clue.text: Errand boy bored by a ship's journey

indicators.note: something bored by another thing has that thing drilled into its middle

parts.note: a page is a boy who runs errands
taken as written
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A young messenger has a long sea voyage on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a voyage by sea or air, as in booking a passage to America.

clue.text: Sick person conspicuous in India? On the contrary

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, with the later phrase flipping which goes inside which
this phrase says the reverse of the stated arrangement holds, so the outer and inner pieces swap roles

parts.note: patent means obvious, plain to see
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Is an ill person easy to spot in India?
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, conspicuous goes in India; 'on the contrary' swaps that, putting India inside conspicuous.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient is someone receiving medical treatment, typically because they are ill.

clue.text: Fight with European finally produces grazes

parts.note: a scrap is a brawl
E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: finally points at the very last letter of the word it governs

parts.note: the final letter of produces

explanation.surface: A brawl involving a European leaves cuts and scratches.
explanation.walkthrough: Produces does double duty: its last letter is used, and it also links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Grazes and scrapes are both minor skin wounds caused by rubbing against a rough surface.

clue.text: Stove hot once more

parts.note: an Aga is a British brand of cast-iron range cooker
hot and in both mean fashionable

explanation.surface: A cooker heats up a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Again and once more both mean another time, a repetition of something.

clue.text: Poignant email not changed, Oscar's admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so one piece goes inside the rest
changed means altered, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written
O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A touching email went out unedited, and Oscar was let in on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Poignant means stirring strong feelings, which is what an emotional scene or speech does.

clue.text: Things sold abroad former lover left with son

indicators.note: with means the following piece is simply added on alongside

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
port is the nautical word for left
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone sells off an ex's belongings overseas, as if after a messy break-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Exports are goods shipped out of a country for sale in foreign markets.

clue.text: Texan golfer regularly gets score of 2 under par

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A golfer from Texas often makes a very good score.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, completing a hole in two strokes fewer than its par is called an eagle.

clue.text: Obvious argument for someone bringing a legal action

parts.note: plain means clear, evident
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A clear-cut case made on behalf of a litigant.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff is the party who sues another in a civil court case.

clue.text: Book about what a waiter might do

parts.note: re means concerning, about
a waiter serves food

explanation.surface: A book about the work of restaurant staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Book looks like a noun for something to read, but it is the verb, as in booking a table.
explanation.definitionFit: To book a table or seat is to reserve it in advance.

clue.text: Shady criminal pauses leaving a court

indicators.note: criminal means crooked or wrong, so the letters are bent out of order
leaving means departing, so a letter goes out of the word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A dodgy offender hesitates as they walk out of court.
explanation.definitionFit: Shady and suspect both describe something of doubtful honesty that arouses mistrust.

clue.text: Fierce wind ripped tops off all dancers outside

parts.note: torn means ripped

indicators.note: the tops of words are their opening letters, taken off to be used

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A violent gale tears the hats off dancers performing in the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violently rotating column of air, the most destructive kind of windstorm.

clue.text: Gossips about student's spectacles

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly
L is a learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: Chatterers comment on how a student's eyewear looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles and glasses are both names for lenses worn in a frame to correct eyesight.

clue.text: Cross and melancholy after end of programme, dear?

indicators.note: after tells us which piece is placed second in the sequence
the end of a word is its final letter only

parts.note: the final letter of programme
a cross is the letter X
pensive means wistfully thoughtful, sad

explanation.surface: Someone is grumpy and gloomy after a show finishes, perhaps about its cost, addressing a loved one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry but is just the letter; 'dear' looks like a term of endearment but means costly.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear in the sense of high-priced, as in petrol being dear this year.

clue.text: Steel section of container vessel

indicators.note: a section is a slice cut out of the longer run of letters that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the join between the two words

explanation.surface: Part of a cargo ship is made from steel.
explanation.walkthrough: Steel looks like the metal of the ship, but here it is a noun for courage, as in steel oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve and steel both mean firm courage or resolve in the face of danger.

clue.text: Tense requests for jobs

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
asks means requests

explanation.surface: Anxious people put in requests for work.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks are pieces of work assigned to someone, just like jobs or chores.

clue.text: Grave vandalised near Tunis

indicators.note: vandalised means smashed up, so the letters are broken and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tomb near the Tunisian capital was defaced.
explanation.walkthrough: Grave looks like a burial site, but it is the adjective meaning solemn.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine means gloomy and serious in temperament, much like grave or sombre.

clue.text: Short woman's dressing gown not oddly slack

indicators.note: something short is cut, so it loses its last letter

parts.note: a negligee is a light woman's dressing gown

indicators.note: oddly means only the letters in odd positions are kept

parts.note: first and third letters of the word

explanation.surface: A skimpy negligee is described as loose-fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Slack here means careless or lax in doing a duty, which is what negligent describes.

clue.text: Big twist, perhaps, extracting Charlie's canine

parts.note: great means big

indicators.note: extracting means pulling out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: the twist is a 1960s dance; perhaps marks it as an example
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A major plot twist drags out Charlie's dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Twist reads as a surprise in a story, but it is the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A Great Dane is a very large breed of dog, so it is an example of a canine.

clue.text: A ballet, e.g. involved light piece of music

indicators.note: involved means complicated or tangled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written without the dots

explanation.surface: A ballet that included a short, light musical number.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagatelle is a short, unpretentious composition, often for piano, like Beethoven's Für Elise.

clue.text: Changes into suits

definitions.meaning: first meaning: turns into something else
second meaning: looks good on, flatters

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone putting on suits; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both turns into, as a caterpillar does a butterfly, and flatters, as a colour does someone.

clue.text: Adult's wife not initially seen in crowd

indicators.note: seen in means appearing inside, so pieces are placed within another

parts.note: a group is a crowd of people
W is the abbreviation for wife

indicators.note: initially points at the first letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the first letter of not

explanation.surface: An adult's wife is not spotted at first among the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up is a fully developed person, an adult as opposed to a child.

clue.text: Looked towards female with wicked daughter

indicators.note: with means the following pieces are added on alongside

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
wicked and ace are both slang for excellent
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A woman turned to her wicked daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Wicked suggests evil, but it is the slang for terrific.
explanation.definitionFit: To face someone is to turn and look in their direction, so faced is looked towards.

clue.text: I left clubs upset with friend's mood

indicators.note: with means the next piece is joined on alongside
upset means overturned; in a down clue that turns letters bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
mate is British slang for friend

explanation.surface: Someone quit their golf clubs in a temper, affecting a friend's mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Climate can mean the prevailing mood or attitude, as in the political climate.

clue.text: Problem after river gets most low

indicators.note: after says the first-named piece comes second in the order

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a pest is a nuisance or problem

explanation.surface: Trouble downstream leaves the river at its lowest level.
explanation.definitionFit: Deepest is the superlative of deep, meaning lying furthest down, the lowest point.

clue.text: Simultaneous combination of notes almost enthralling one group of singers

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so one piece is held inside
almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: a chord is several notes sounded together
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A harmony nearly captivates a group of vocalists.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is an organised body of singers, as in a church or school.

clue.text: Put off by tunnel's mould

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so the second piece sits next to the first

parts.note: to deter is to discourage
a mine is an underground tunnel

explanation.surface: Someone is put off by the mould growing in a tunnel.
explanation.walkthrough: Mould looks like fungus, but it is a verb meaning to shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine something can mean to shape or decide its form, as circumstances mould events.

clue.text: Poet finished penning note

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as animals are held in a pen

parts.note: done means finished
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: A poet has finished writing a note.
explanation.walkthrough: Penning looks like writing, fitting a poet, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: John Donne was an English metaphysical poet of the early seventeenth century.

clue.text: Small animal climbing long grasses

indicators.note: climbing means going upward, which in a down clue reads the letters bottom to top

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a deer is an animal

explanation.surface: A little creature scrambles up through tall vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeds are tall grass-like plants that grow in wet ground, the tall grasses of marshes.

clue.text: Soldiers not retreating around island state

parts.note: men are ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse
around means surrounding, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: taken as written
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Troops hold their ground around an island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: State looks like a nation, matching island, but it is a verb meaning to say.
explanation.definitionFit: To mention something is to state or refer to it briefly in speech.

clue.text: Mediocre answer doctor gave her missing husband

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged
missing means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A doctor gave a woman a so-so answer, without her husband present.
explanation.definitionFit: Average describes something ordinary and unremarkable, neither good nor bad, much like mediocre.

clue.text: Final drink, remember? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means only half is kept, the rest being dropped

parts.note: to sup is to drink
taken as written

explanation.surface: A last drink, and a rhetorical query about memory answered with the British exclamation 'not half!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', but here it literally cuts the word in half.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means highest in authority, so a supreme court's ruling is the final word.

clue.text: Far end of theatre? Moving seat is most simple

indicators.note: the far end of a word is its very last letter

parts.note: the final letter of theatre

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatregoer at the back finds swapping seats the simplest option.
explanation.definitionFit: Easiest is the superlative of easy, meaning the least difficult or most straightforward.
